gloss: naturally; of itself; in the nature of things

definitions.gloss: naturally; of its own accord; as a matter of course
definitions.explanation: Describes an outcome that follows naturally from the way things are, without anyone forcing it. Literary and somewhat elevated; common in essays, aphorisms, and formal speech.

examples.japanese: {答|こた}えはおのずから{明|あき}らかだ。
{続|つづ}けていれば、おのずから{道|みち}は{開|ひら}ける。
examples.english: If you keep at it, a path will open up of its own accord.

examples.japanese: {立場|たちば}が{変|か}われば、{物事|ものごと}の{見|み}え{方|かた}もおのずから{変|か}わってくる。
examples.english: When your position changes, the way things look naturally changes with it.

notes:
Also written {自|おの}ずから. The literary variant of おのずと, with which it is interchangeable in most contexts; おのずから sounds a shade more formal and is preferred in writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- おのずから{明|あき}らかだ: is naturally obvious
- おのずから{分|わ}かる: will become clear in due course
- おのずから{限界|げんかい}がある: there are natural limits

SIMILAR WORDS:
- おのずと: naturally — the same word in its ordinary modern form
- {自然|しぜん}と: naturally — the casual everyday counterpart
- ひとりでに: by itself — about the absence of an agent, not about a natural course of events
